results.name: PAYLOAD ransomware attacks through Active Directory GPO
results.description: In April 2026, a manufacturing organization in the Middle East suffered a ransomware attack where threat actors with domain admin privileges weaponized Active Directory Group Policy Objects to achieve domain-wide impact without deploying ransomware binaries on Windows endpoints. The attackers created malicious GPOs linked at the domain root, delivering ransom notes, hijacking wallpapers and lock screens, enforcing logon banners, and disabling local administrator accounts across all domain-joined workstations. No file encryption occurred on Windows systems; instead, the operation focused on encryptionless extortion through operational disruption and data exfiltration. Initial access was gained via compromised VPN credentials. The attack remained dormant for one day between GPO creation and detonation, evading file-based detection entirely by abusing trusted AD infrastructure.

results.name: Don't Call Us, We'll Call Your APIs | TraderTraitor Backdoors Resurface on Victim With No Crypto Ties
results.description: In 2026, the DPRK-sponsored Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor continued campaigns targeting cryptocurrency entities, including a high-profile attack on LayerZero resulting in $292 million theft from KelpDAO. Following this disclosure, an additional victim was identified: a smaller IT services provider in India with no cryptocurrency connections. The compromise involved a DevOps engineer targeted through fake job interview lures containing weaponized Terraform coding projects. Malicious GitHub repositories used typosquatted provider domains to deliver macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK when victims executed terraform init. The backdoors enabled reconnaissance, credential theft, and cloud environment escalation. One day after LayerZero's public disclosure, attackers deployed an updated stripped version of ROOFDECK and removed earlier implants. Activity continued until June 2026, suggesting the threat actor ultimately abandoned the intrusion after determining insufficient value from the smaller target.

results.name: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257
results.description: Active exploitation of PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 has been observed, targeting GlobalProtect portal and gateway components. The authentication bypass flaw allows unauthorized attackers to circumvent security controls and establish VPN connections. Ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), along with Settra ransomware actors, are exploiting this vulnerability to gain initial network access. Following successful exploitation, threat actors bypass multi-factor authentication, conduct internal reconnaissance using remote monitoring tools, move laterally via RDP and SMB, and stage additional tooling for credential harvesting and ransomware deployment. A sophisticated tactic observed involves pivoting directly to the virtualization layer, accessing vCenter management appliances, disabling security controls on ESXi hypervisors, and performing offline credential dumping against domain controller virtual disks. results.name: Ukraine's State Data-Exchange System Targeted by Russian-Speaking Operator via Graylog Log4Shell
results.description: Between May and September 2026, a Russian-speaking operator systematically targeted Ukraine's state data-exchange infrastructure by exploiting Log4Shell vulnerabilities in Graylog servers. The attacker swept 9.1 million Ukrainian IP addresses, filtering 7,576 live hosts to identify systems running UXP Verifier, a component of the national data-exchange platform. Using a two-stage CommonsBeanutils2 deserialization chain delivered through Graylog's sessions API, the operator gained access to at least two organizations, including a logging server containing 6.8 million documents from Ukraine's state data-exchange system. The operation was exposed when the attacker accidentally served their working directory over HTTP for 17 hours, revealing reconnaissance tools, shell history, exploit code, and access logs. While the operator queried transaction indices and demonstrated prior knowledge of the system's schema, no data exfiltration was directly observed. results.name: Midnight Mimosa Malware Campaign Exploits Android Firmware Supply Chain
results.description: Midnight Mimosa is a widespread Android malware campaign involving malicious applications preinstalled in firmware of low-cost MediaTek-based devices, with infections observed across more than 150 countries. The campaign leverages platform-signed system applications to silently deploy payloads, evade mobile security protections, execute remotely supplied code, and monetize compromised devices through advertising fraud and residential-proxy services. The malicious firmware components provide persistent system-level access before device activation, bypass conventional Android security controls by temporarily disabling Google Play Store protections, and maintain privileged positions while operators rotate payloads remotely. Affected devices include low-cost Android handsets, counterfeit flagship models, and devices associated with Doogee and Cubot products, with highest concentrations reported in Mexico, France, and Italy.

results.name: Inside Wazza: A Newly Observed Device Code Phishing Kit Targeting Microsoft 365 Accounts
results.description: A newly observed multi-stage phishing kit named Wazza has been actively targeting Microsoft 365 accounts since early July 2026. The campaign delivers phishing emails from compromised accounts containing PDF lures with business themes like invoices and contracts. These PDFs redirect victims through a complex infrastructure leveraging Google Sites, CloudFlare Workers, and various domains. Wazza features dynamic capabilities including 19 different phishing themes impersonating services like Adobe, DocuSign, and OneDrive, along with six corporate decoy websites. The kit employs sophisticated browser interrogation, anti-automation checks, and client-side protection mechanisms. The final stage abuses Microsoft OAuth device authorization, displaying a verification code and instructing victims to complete authentication on a separate page. Throughout the process, a backend session continuously monitors the authentication attempt, ultimately granting attackers access to victim accounts and cloud resources.

results.name: From Phishing to LLMjacking: Threat Actors Targeting Cloud Billing Accounts for LLM Usage
results.description: Threat actors are conducting sophisticated campaigns targeting Google Cloud Platform environments through phishing attacks via sponsored search ads. Attackers compromise privileged user credentials using fake login pages, then manipulate organizational policies to disable security guardrails. They create service accounts with Gemini API access, invite external attacker-controlled accounts, and assign administrative billing roles. The attackers link their external GCP projects to victim billing accounts, enabling them to execute large-scale AI workloads while hiding activity from victim monitoring. This results in unauthorized charges reaching tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars within 24-48 hours. The campaigns employ evasion techniques including geographic IP blending and demoting legitimate administrators to prevent detection and remediation.

results.name: Dissection of Operation FlashHole, a complex attack by Lazarus
results.description: In January, Lazarus Group launched Operation FlashHole against South Korea, exploiting mandatory security software CrossWeb EX through watering hole strategies and targeted spear-phishing emails with fake portfolio and resume sites. The campaign began in July the previous year, targeting software, construction, and cable equipment manufacturing sectors. The attack chain combines old and new malware families including TechHub, Cubridge, TouchShift, TouchHub, ClientHub, and LPEClient. Notable techniques include in-memory execution, GitHub and Dropbox for command-and-control infrastructure, DLL side-loading, and the incorporation of post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-1024) and GOST encryption. The sophisticated modular framework demonstrates Lazarus's continuous evolution of tools and tactics specifically designed for South Korean targets.

results.name: The Gentlemen: A closer look at a not-so-gentle ransomware-as-a-service operation
results.description: The Gentlemen is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in mid-2025 after operating as an affiliate of LockBit and Qilin. The group offers affiliates up to 90% of ransom revenue and has claimed over 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors. The ransomware targets Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems using a double-extortion model that encrypts files and exfiltrates data. Written in Go, the ransomware employs ChaCha20 encryption with multiple speed modes, terminates security processes using vulnerable drivers, and spreads laterally through networks via PsExec. A May 2026 infrastructure breach exposed internal communications, affiliate information, and connections to the Qilin ecosystem. Organizations in the United States and Europe are most frequently targeted, particularly in manufacturing, technology, healthcare, professional services, and retail sectors.

results.name: Active Exploitation of CVE-2026-110936 in Siemens Software Center
results.description: A DLL side-loading vulnerability in Software Center version 3.5.8.7 is being actively exploited by attackers. The threat actors distribute a genuine, digitally signed copy of the application alongside malicious DLL files through unofficial channels. When executed, the vulnerable version loads the attacker-supplied DLLs without validation, enabling malicious code execution. The attack vector involves ClickFix social engineering tactics, tricking users into executing commands. The campaign uses specific infrastructure for payload hosting and command-and-control operations. Version 4.0.9.8 patches this vulnerability, with automatic updates applied upon application restart. No official systems or distribution channels were compromised during this campaign.
